maildoc

maildoc reads and writes the portable mail document defined by the mail document decision. It uses bus's wire parser with the client feature disabled. Opening a document never sends mail. The library does no file access or transport work; Email checks sender identities and real addresses when sending.

The source is libs/maildoc.

API and format

parse(&str) -> Result<MailDocument, Refusal> reads the document; write(&MailDocument) -> Result<String, Refusal> serialises it; validate(&MailDocument) -> Result<(), Refusal> checks canonical fields and encoded size for Email and ced without file I/O. MailDocument derives Default, Clone, Debug, PartialEq and Eq.

---
mail-attachments: ["/home/user/report.pdf"]
mail-from: ann@example.org
mail-references: <first@example.org> <parent@example.org>
mail-subject: "[PATCH] build notes"
mail-to: Alice <alice@example.com>, bob@example.org
---
Hi Alice,

The **build** is ready.

Only these nine names are accepted:

HeaderFieldOn disk
mail-to, mail-cc, mail-bccVec<String>Comma-separated addresses, each trimmed; display text retained
mail-from, mail-reply-toOption<String>One address as written
mail-subjectStringSubject text
mail-in-reply-toOption<String>Parent message ID
mail-referencesVec<String>Whitespace-separated message IDs, in order
mail-attachmentsVec<PathBuf>JSON array of absolute UTF-8 paths; never opened

Address validation here checks only that each entry is non-empty and contains @, is trimmed and contains no comma. Commas always separate list entries, including commas inside display names; full RFC address parsing belongs to Email.

An ordinary value starting with " must be a JSON string and is decoded. Other ordinary values are taken as written after the wire parser trims them; even an unquoted [PATCH] is accepted. The wire parser's advisory JSON errors do not reject ordinary mail text. Attachments must always be a valid JSON array of strings, never a JSON string containing an array. Decoded values, including each attachment path, must contain no control characters (including CR, LF and tab). Raw header values have the same restriction.

Every other header is refused by name, including unknown mail-* names and all routing or broker names. Malformed and duplicate header lines are refused before the lenient parser can skip or overwrite them. Empty values, including "" and bare mail-subject:, are refused; omit the header instead. Empty lists are accepted and disappear when written. Both fences are required. Any CR anywhere in the document, including bare CR and CRLF, has a separate Refusal::CarriageReturn error with guidance to use LF.

Input larger than MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (8 MiB, the broker relay frame cap) is refused with Refusal::TooLarge. The bound counts UTF-8 bytes for the complete document, including framing; exactly 8 MiB is accepted. It applies locally too.

Writing and round trips

The writer sorts headers through bus::wire::BusMessage, omits empty or absent values, and uses LF framing. It JSON-quotes ordinary values beginning with [, { or ", or carrying leading/trailing Unicode whitespace. Attachment arrays remain JSON arrays. The body is appended exactly as supplied, with no extra final newline. An empty header block includes a blank line between its fences so the Bus parser can read a body following it; compact empty blocks are accepted on read too.

Reading normalises these details:

  • Unquoted values lose leading/trailing Unicode whitespace; quoted strings retain it. Address-list entries are trimmed after decoding.
  • Address separators become comma plus space when written. Reference separators become one space. Their original separator bytes are not kept.
  • The entire body's trailing Unicode whitespace is removed by wire::parse_lenient: spaces at the very end and trailing blank lines disappear. Leading whitespace and interior line endings/spaces survive.

For example, a body hello \n\n reads as hello. Before writing that parsed document, the caller gets the normalised body hello. The writer refuses a body with trailing whitespace rather than silently changing its content.

write refuses non-canonical input. Header values contain no controls; all address entries (including From/Reply-To) are trimmed, non-empty, contain @ and no comma; optional strings are non-empty; reference entries are non-empty whitespace-free tokens; attachment paths are absolute UTF-8 without controls; the body has no CR or trailing whitespace; and the encoded document fits 8 MiB, including any expansion from JSON quoting. Non-UTF-8 paths return InvalidValue { header: "mail-attachments", reason: "path is not UTF-8" }. Parsing applies the same checks after normalisation. Every successful write parses back to an equal document: parse(&write(&d)?)? == d.

Adding these names to bus::wire::KNOWN_HEADERS only silences advisory validate() warnings. This crate's allowlist enforces the document boundary.

Tests

Run cargo test -p maildoc -p bus --locked through the build cluster. Unit tests cover refusals, quoting, normalisation, framing, sorted headers and the relay bound; proptest checks canonical document round-trip equality and that arbitrary documents either fail writing or round-trip unchanged.
